# SoundSnatcher

> A free, open-source local tool that converts a YouTube link into an MP3 or WAV file and
> writes the detected BPM and musical key directly into the download filename. Built for
> DJs and music producers who organise libraries by tempo and key.

Homepage: https://bohanl1u.github.io/SoundSnatcher/
Source: https://github.com/bohanl1u/SoundSnatcher
Licence: MIT
Cost: free, no paid tier, no account

## What it does

Paste a YouTube link, press one button, and download the audio. Optionally tick "Analyze
key & BPM" and the file arrives named like `Track Name - 128BPM - Fmin.mp3`, which sorts
correctly in a DJ library without a tag editor. Each key detection also reports its
Camelot code for harmonic mixing.

Output formats:
- MP3 at 128, 192, 256 or 320 kbps (LAME, 44.1 kHz)
- WAV at 16-bit, 44.1 kHz

The source audio is downloaded once per link; changing format re-encodes locally rather
than downloading again.

## How to install

Requires Node 20 or newer, plus `yt-dlp` and `ffmpeg` on the PATH.

```
brew install node yt-dlp ffmpeg
git clone https://github.com/bohanl1u/SoundSnatcher.git
cd SoundSnatcher
npm install
npm start
```

It then runs at http://localhost:4747. `npm run doctor` verifies the external binaries are
found.

## Why it runs locally rather than as a hosted website

YouTube heavily rate-limits datacenter IP addresses, so a cloud-hosted version fails
frequently while a local one works normally on a home connection. Running locally is also
faster (no upload step, no queue) and imposes no limit on video length.

## Analysis accuracy

Measured against 17 reference tracks whose BPM and key are stated by their producers:

- BPM: 14 of 17 exact, 3 octave-off (half or double time), 0 otherwise wrong.
- Key: 8 of 14 exact, 1 fifth-error.

Tempo detection is reliable. Key detection should be treated as a hint rather than a
verdict: relative major and minor keys share six of seven notes, and material with no
third present has no mode to detect. Half and double-time readings are often a genre
convention rather than an error — drill is written at 140 BPM and felt at 70.

Method: tempo comes from a spectral-flux onset envelope, autocorrelation, and comb-filter
scoring weighted by a log-normal prior. Key comes from a chroma vector built from
interpolated spectral peaks, correlated against Sha'ath's key profiles. Both are
implemented in plain JavaScript with no native dependencies.

## Privacy

No accounts, no tracking, no telemetry. The tool runs on the user's own machine and the
links pasted into it are not sent anywhere except to fetch the audio.

## Intended use

Only for audio the user has the rights to use. SoundSnatcher is not affiliated with
YouTube or Google.
